newsitem.title: EGYPT: SOCCER-FINANCIAL WOES HIT AFRICA'S OLDEST CUP COMPETITION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FINANCIAL WOES HIT AFRICA'S OLDEST CUP COMPETITION.

text.p: The format of Africa's oldest surviving competition, the East and Central African Senior Challenge Cup, is to be changed as mounting financial problems catch up with competing countries.

The annual event, to which countries belonging to the regonal Confederation of East and Central African Football Associations (CECAFA) are invited, is now to be held every two years after just six of its 14 members turned up for this year's event.
CECAFA chairman Tesfaye Gebreyesus confirmed in Cairo on Wednesday that the next event would be held in Rwanda in 1998, breaking with a tradition that stretches back to 1927.
"We have to change because there is a lot of pressures on the member countries, who also have commitments in the World Cup and African Nations' Cup qualifiers," he said.
Uganda won the tournament in Sudan in November which saw several last-minute withdrawals and the hosts having to enter their under-20 team to make up the numbers.
CECAFA have also postponed their annual club championship by a month to February because of international commitments in January for many of the participating players.
But the association will still go ahead with its new under-20 championship in Uganda in April, Gebreyesus said.
"Football in our region is not up to previous standards and we have to develop the youth for the future," he said.
